title: Reject text index with min_token_len greater than max_token_len
body:
## Summary

Fixes #10578 — a full-text index configured with `min_token_len > max_token_len` is accepted by both REST and gRPC, but the token filter then rejects every token, silently building an empty index.

This change rejects the inverted range at validation time, mirroring the existing integer-index `lookup`/`range` check.

## Changes

- **`lib/segment/src/data_types/index.rs`**: add `validate_text_index_params` and a `Validate` impl for `TextIndexParams`.
- **`lib/segment/src/types.rs`**: wire `TextIndexParams::validate` into `PayloadSchemaParams::validate` (REST path).
- **`lib/api/src/grpc/validate.rs`**: add a `Validate` impl for the gRPC `TextIndexParams` and call it from `IndexParams::validate`.
- **`lib/edge/ffi/src/payload_index.rs`**: enforce the same rule in the FFI conversion (returns `InvalidArgument`).
- **Tests**: unit test for `validate_text_index_params` and an OpenAPI regression test asserting a 422 with the new error message.

## Testing

- Unit test covers valid (`min < max`, `min == max`, unset) and invalid (`min > max`) cases.
- OpenAPI test asserts `PUT /collections/{name}/index` with `min_token_len: 10, max_token_len: 5` returns 422.

Note: I was unable to run `cargo test` locally (no Rust toolchain installed), so CI will need to confirm compilation and tests.

title: Allow in-place enable_hnsw updates on payload indexes
body:
## Summary
- Refactor payload-index schema transitions from `OnlyOnDiskFlipped` to `Compatible(CompatibleDiff)`, so `on_disk` and `enable_hnsw` flips (including combinations) share one shape instead of per-combination variants.
- Treat `enable_hnsw` as metadata-only: keep existing field-index files and persist the updated schema, instead of drop-and-rebuild from payload.
- Preserve existing `on_disk` behavior (reuse on non-appendable; drop-and-rebuild on appendable).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p segment --lib schema_transition`
- [x] `cargo test -p segment --lib struct_payload_index::tests`
- [ ] Confirm create-index with `enable_hnsw: true → false` on a live collection updates schema without rebuilding postings
- [ ] Confirm next HNSW rebuild skips additional links for fields with `enable_hnsw: false`

title: test(segment): pin graph_inline_storage HNSW build to 1 CPU and seed 42
body:
## Problem

`test_graph_inline_storage_contract::case_3_u8` (Uint8 + Mmap) is flaky in CI. The assertion at line 277 (`common + 2 >= TOP`, TOP=10) needs 8 of the 10 exact nearest neighbors in the approximate result. The reported failure on 2026-09-24 had only 6 in common:

```
[103, 132, 161, 288, 347, 366, 473, 543, 565, 595] vs [132, 153, 161, 173, 366, 432, 473, 543, 565, 595]
```

## Root cause

The input vectors are already seeded (`StdRng::seed_from_u64(4242)`), but the HNSW graph built for the indexed segment is not deterministic. `build_indexed` calls `SegmentBuilder::build_for_test`, which does two things:

- It passes `ResourcePermit::dummy(get_num_indexing_threads(0))`, so the permit covers every CPU on the machine. The graph build pool is sized from `permit.num_cpus` (`lib/segment/src/index/hnsw_index/hnsw/build.rs:146`), not from `max_indexing_threads` in the test config. Setting that field to 1 does not make the build single-threaded.
- It uses an unseeded `rand::rng()`, and point levels are drawn from that RNG (`build.rs:161`).

So the graph changes from run to run and from runner to runner. For the Uint8 case the recall margin is small enough that some graphs miss the threshold.

My first version of this PR pinned `max_indexing_threads` to 1. That was wrong for the reason above, and it is reverted here.

## Fix

`build_indexed` now calls `SegmentBuilder::build` directly with `ResourcePermit::dummy(1)` and `StdRng::seed_from_u64(42)`. With one CPU and a fixed seed, the graph is the same on every run. `max_indexing_threads` is back to 2, as on `dev`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p segment --test integration graph_inline_storage_test::test_graph_inline_storage_contract`: all 6 cases pass.
- I ran `case_3_u8` 20 times with the fix on a GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` runner: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- For reference, the unfixed test also passed 20/20 on the same runner, so the flake did not show up on that machine. The fix removes both sources of variation rather than relying on the failure rate being low.
- `cargo +nightly fmt --all --check`: clean.

## Scope

Test-only change. No production code touched.

Fixes #10774

title: [Feature Request]: Nano (XNO) payment for Qdrant Cloud Inference API
body:
## Describe the problem

Qdrant Cloud's Inference API uses paid models for embeddings (remote inference with `cloud_inference=True`). Users are billed for inference tokens — a metered, per-token API that AI agents call at high frequency. For autonomous agents that need per-operation payment authority, paying for each inference request in USD or USDC means per-transaction fees that make micropayments uneconomical.

The Qdrant Python client (`qdrant-client`) already supports inference via `Document` models — `client.upsert(collection_name, points=[PointStruct(id=1, payload={\"topic\": \"cooking\"}, vector=Document(text=\"...\", model=\"<model>\"))])`. Each such call triggers a paid inference. Agents that embed at scale accumulate many such micropayments.

## Describe the proposed solution

Add **Nano (XNO) payment support** for Qdrant Cloud's Inference API, integrated through the client library.

Concretely:

1. **A Nano-payment-aware client option** that intercepts inference calls (when `cloud_inference=True` and a model is specified), derives a per-request Nano payment via x402 (using the existing feeless402 library — `github.com/michardnicolas/feeless402`), and submits the payment before the inference call. Drop-in: `client = QdrantClient(url=..., api_key=..., cloud_inference=True, payment='nano')` instead of the current constructor.

2. **For Qdrant**: accept Nano as a billing currency for inference tokens. Agents that already hold XNO can pay for inference without converting to USD, avoiding fee erosion that makes sub-cent micropayments uneconomical.

## Alternatives considered

- **USDC on Base via x402**: gas fees exceed micropayment value.
- **Credit card billing**: aggregated monthly — not per-operation.
- **Do nothing**: agents infer until the bill comes due.

## Importance

- **would make my life easier** — high-frequency embedding workloads where each inference should be paid for in real time by the agent itself.

## Additional context

- `feeless402` (MIT) provides fee-free x402 micropayments in Nano — `github.com/michardnicolas/feeless402`.
- Nano: fee-free, <1s settlement, self-custodied.
- A working Nano x402 adapter for the OpenAI Agents SDK exists — `github.com/dhyabi2/openai-agents-nano-x402`.
